utterances.text: I do. Radic, aka Roda -- Mladen Radic, aka Roda.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mladen Radovic, aka Roda?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you know who was his deputy?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours, please, I'm not objecting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not objecting. It's just that it's important to the Prosecution to have the transcript clear. In line 9, page 44, there was a name that came before Maslic. I think it was something like Cvijetin. I wonder if that could be clarified because I've heard that name before and I want to check it out in the transcript later tonight or tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can confirm that, because I don't believe this is the time when the -- when the translators do not catch the name. But actually, I will clarify again this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you say that this was Cvijetin Maslic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps confirm that Jovo Savic that we already mentioned once in relation to the 4th Detachment as the deputy commander? He was in fact later the deputy commander of the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, the Army of Republika Srpska was established on the 12th of May, 1992. I believe that this is not contested by the Prosecution. I believe this is the official date when the Army of Republika Srpska was established. So that was in May 1992. Could you confirm that by the establishment of the 5th Battalion, the 4th Detachment ceased to exist on the 12th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not cease to exist. The 4th Detachment continued to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was it from then on perhaps called 5th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it was called, but it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that we have dealt with this topic of the 4th Detachment enough. I would now like to go on to another topic very briefly. On the night of the 16th to the 17th of April -- and I believe that this date is now uncontested in this case -- there was armed conflict that broke out in Bosanski Samac. According to your statement, you heard shooting but you stayed in your house because you were frightened of going out. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, can we again please be specific. If you mean his evidence in court, according to his testimony, or is it his statement which you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do have in mind. Now I'm talking about his testimony before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In Court. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, was your brother, Esad Dagovic, also in the house that night? Did he remain in the house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did he leave the house perhaps?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the entire night your brother stayed in the house.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What about your father? Did he also stay in the house all night?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That night passed, and there was the day of the 17th of April. You said that you set off for work but that you saw soldiers, that you were frightened and you returned home.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You also said during the examination-in-chief -- you said that you were employed, that you worked at the amusement gate, that this was property of Muhamed Bicic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is my assumption. But perhaps you correct me if I'm wrong. Such amusement arcades -- games arcades do not start work so early in the morning. Could you tell me what the time was when you set off for work.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 9.00 in the morning, 9.30 perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And at that time when you set off for work and later on in the course of the morning, did you see Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What about Hasan Bicic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So that morning, the 17th of April, you did not see Muhamed and Hasan Bicic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you and your brother, you worked in the establishment of Mr. Bicic. We heard that already. And as far as I understand, your relations with the Bicic brothers were more than just employer/employee relations. Am I right in saying that with the Bicic brothers, you and your brother were as a matter of fact close friends?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We were close friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you knew the families of Muhamed and Hasan Bicic. You knew their wives -- Muhamed's wife, Hasan's wife, the children, and all of them, their mother, their father; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did their families in town in Samac on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter corrects herself. Were their families in town in Samac on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After the 17th, did you see them in Samac later on?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could I pause for one second, because I think that there's something in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, you told me that you were close friends with Muhamed and Hasan Bicic. I presume that you will be able to answer the following question, considering this relations that you had with them. Did Hasan Bicic own an automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What about Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like us to go to another topic. I would like to ask you a couple of questions in relation to your father. Your father is Sabrija Dagovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the time when the conflict broke out in April 1992, could you tell me approximately how old was your father?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 54, 55 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So we could say that he was middle-aged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, he was a worker in the textile industry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: An honest and honourable man, respected in the -- in his -- in the area where he was living and working; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your father never had any convictions. He did not commit any incidents. He had no misdemeanour record. He lived all his life as an honourable and respected citizen of Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He's not a man who would lie, is he, or do some other immoral things; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, do you know that your father gave a statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you and your brother present when your father gave a statement?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, do you know that your father said in his statement that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours, please, I object to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Particularly, as it can only lead one place, and that is to ask this witness to comment on what his father says in another document. It's not for this witness to explain what other people say in other documents. He can only answer questions himself directly. And it seems to me that this question: Do you know that your father said in his statement whatever can only lead to that particular topic and otherwise wouldn't make any sense. So I object to the question, and I particularly object to the question because it's going to -- it can only go to that issue of asking him to comment on what his father says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I can reply to my learned colleague. I didn't ask the witness still and I have no intention to ask him to comment the statement of some other witness. I will wait for that. I am just asking him whether he knows what -- that his father said this and this. This question is not ask for comment. This is question: Do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And I believe that this question is quite proper. On the other hand, having in mind that this statement has already been discussed, that the Trial Chamber is aware of the content of this statement, and that there is a ruling in this regard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the fairness of trial would allow me at least to ask him do you know that your father said this. That's all I have intention to ask about this statement. And that's absolutely all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No any more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If that is all, then that is all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And I just want to remind you that you do recall the limited purpose for which the statement was admitted by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, do you know that your father said that his two sons -- presumably he means you and Esad -- were in a group of people who offered resistance in the course of the first day that both his sons had weapons and that they took part in the combat in town and that they returned on Saturday morning at 9.30 on the 18th of April, 1992? Now, the question is only: Do you know that this is what your father said?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dagovic, let us go on to the 18th of April. According to your testimony, soldiers came in front of your house to collect weapons. That was on the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You also said that they called you and your brother to come out into the yard. That's what it says in the transcript, page 7111. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From this I can conclude that at the moment that when the soldiers arrived, you and your brother were in the house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So both of you, who were in the house itself.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony during the examination-in-chief, you said that -- that the soldiers were accompanied by a tank and that you saw Simo Zaric and Miroslav Tadic standing on the tank with a few other soldiers. Now, in relation to what you said, I would like to ask you a couple of questions. Mr. Dagovic, do you know what BOV is, a military term? You were in the army, so that's why I'm asking you. Perhaps you know.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what BOV is.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a kind of a machine-gun, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was going to tell you that this is an APC. Actually, it is an abbreviation for an armoured personnel carrier. But I see that that wouldn't lead anywhere. But perhaps I could ask you what is Praga?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A type of a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Praga is an anti-aircraft armoured vehicle. But again, you don't have to know this. But this vehicle that according to you came before your house, was that a tank or was it a BOV, or was it a Praga? Was it another military vehicle which was -- which had a military purpose? Perhaps it was an anti-aircraft vehicle. Was it an armoured vehicle? Was it really a tank?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With the permission of Your Honours, I would like to show to the witness one photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This photograph is actually the same one as D17/4. But since the -- D16/4, I'm sorry. And I already referred to the Registry, and we compared these photographs, and they believe can confirm this. It's the same photograph. The only difference is that this photograph is not marked. And so I believe that this one is more appropriate to be used in cross-examination, since D16/4 is marked already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we confirm from the Registry assistant. Is it the same photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it is indeed the first -- the same photograph, D16/4 it was marked before, and it responds to the photo currently held by counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: May I see the one that's being presented to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then for purposes of the record, can we say that it is a fresh copy of D16/4?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. And I assume that we need a fresh copy because it's going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: My learned friend is going to ask the witness to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. Well, in that case, I've got no problem with another copy being used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, you can see before you on the ELMO, you can see on the screen before you can see a photograph. And now I would like to ask you to -- about the identification of what we see before us. This is Pere Bosnica Street is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Pere Bosnica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This white house that we can see is the house that is located in front of the family house. Is that you're house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So this is your yard surrounding this house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your house is located inside the yard, and we cannot see it from here on this photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to ask you one thing. You mentioned the tank. And the first question would be: When was the first time that you saw that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a noise. The tank was going down the street. And I saw the tank moving down the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you saw it going down the street.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From which direction was the tank coming?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the direction of the Social Services. That is, from up there towards town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's exactly what I want from you. So could you take a marker and just on the street, on this Pere Bosnica Street, if you could mark it with an arrow the direction from which the tank came.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From left to right or right to left. That's all I was asking you to do. If you can mark the arrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may the record reflect that the arrow marked that the witness had just pointed shows the direction where the tank came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's arrow marked on the photograph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, I don't need this photograph any more. And may I have the number for this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can have the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is D22/4, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So sir, I've already asked you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I just want to make sure with the registry assistant that the marking won't come off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's hope that it is or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because I'm wondering about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The quality of the marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It will remain? It won't come off?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes, counsel, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My colleague already asked you about the statement you gave to the investigators of the OTP on the 12th of September, 1992. And I asked you a number of questions related to that statement. But let us clarify certain things right here and now. You gave that statement of your own free will; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the statement recorded exactly what you said to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: They didn't force you to say anything.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After the statement was drawn up in writing, was it read out to you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And again, of your own free will you signed the statement and put your initials on every page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I suppose I will need some assistance from my colleagues from the Prosecution in this. But let me point out one thing I've noticed when reading your statement. You never mention the incident involving the tank. You never mentioned the word "tank." And I will now read out to you your own description of that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is on page 1, paragraph 4. "When they came to my house on 18th April, 1992, Goran Buzakovic and Fadil Topcagic demanded that I hand over my weapons. They had with them a list of people that had hunting licences. Fadil Topcagic asked my brother to hand over his weapon. My brother had a pistol, which he had a permit for. My brother also owned a 72 automatic gun, and I don't know if that weapon was registered or not. After we gave them the guns - plural - they left. Simo Zaric and Miroslav Tadic did nothing while at our house other than stand in our garden and demand that we hand over our weapons. The four of them went from house to house demanding weapons."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, that is the version I've already asked you about. In fact, I asked to -- I asked you to confirm that that was the case. But you never mentioned a tank before. You're mentioning it for the first time after ten years.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is as I described it. And I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you wait, pause, counsel. The interpretation hasn't completed the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is another detail, namely the 72 millimetres automatic weapon. I suppose that is supposed to be 7.62 millimetres, and the weapon belonged to your brother who turned it over on that occasion, which differs from your testimony. Is your statement correct, namely that your brother owned an automatic weapon of the 7.62 millimetres caliber, or is your testimony correct saying that he only had a pistol?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He only had a pistol. But if you read the statement more closely, you will see that it was a 72 millimetres pistol, automatic pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But isn't it true that in your interview with the Prosecutor just before coming here to testify, you said also that your brother had an automatic weapon?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I said that he only had a pistol, for which he had a licence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Then I suppose my learned friends from the Prosecution misunderstood what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours, please, he can't comment on what the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Understood or did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, in the basement of your house beneath the pile of coal, had there been an automatic rifle that your brother turned over to soldier Goran Buzakovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon of any kind?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You were already asked by the Prosecution about your place of residence, and you answered that you lived in one of the west European countries. Without mentioning the name of the country, is it the same country that your brother Esad resides in?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you live in the same town or city?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have a good relationship with your brother?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see each other, visit each other. Your families are friendly.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you have a truly brothers relationship. You trust each other in everything.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you lie for the sake of your brother?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever discussed your or his testimony with your brother?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With your own brother, with whom you are good brothers, you never spoke a word about the fact that he testified before this Tribunal and that you too were supposed to testify.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about it in general, but we didn't talk about our testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, did you perhaps harmonise your testimony with his to protect his credibility?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Why would I?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have only a few more questions to ask you. You have described an incident which took place when members of Serb special forces came to your house accompanied by Hasan Bicic and demanded money. You said that they drove your brother's car away on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to know if possible when exactly that happened. Was it -- was this vehicle in the possession of your brother in this period that started on the 16th or the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was it in the garage of your house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Relative to the 16th or the 18th of April, when this conflict broke out, how many days after the outbreak of the conflict did these members of the special forces come to your house with Hasan Bicic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came on the 28th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 28th of April? Are you saying that it couldn't have been on the 20th of April, two days after the collection of weapons?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was -- that's impossible. It couldn't have been then?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There are a couple of more -- a couple of things more that I want to clarify. One of them has to do with this collection of weapons that was carried out by the army. In response to the Prosecutor's question as to the accused Zaric's dress, you said that he was wearing a camouflage uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, it was only on the 27th of April that Mr. Zaric received a camouflage uniform. Until then, he had a JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. He had a camouflage uniform on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There remains one topic I will deal with briefly. It has to do with the meetings held at the memorial hall. And today from your testimony I understood there were two such meetings where Muslims and Croats were invited to join the VRS. You said that the second meeting took place somewhere in August or September 1992, but I didn't understand when the first meeting was.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June or July. I couldn't tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Generally it fits in the time frame mentioned by some other witnesses. However, as far as the speech made on that occasion is concerned, we have heard witnesses who said that this speech inviting Muslims and Croats to join was made by Jovo Savic, deputy command of the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was made by Simo Zaric. Perhaps there was another speech --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The answer has come in. Perhaps I'm too late on getting to my feet. But it's the same problem, witness -- sorry, counsel asking the witness to comment on what other witnesses have said. Essentially, that's the thrust of the question. All he can say -- all this witness can be asked is well, who do you remember making the speech?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It's okay, because the witness can agree or disagree and give his own narration of the information he knows. So there's nothing wrong with the question as it has been put.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. No, there's nothing wrong with asking the witness, look, you're mistaken. It was in fact Jovo Savic who gave the speech. No problem with that at all. What is a problem is saying look, other witnesses have said that. Now, what do you say? That's the effect of it. And that's what I'm concerned about, because it puts pressure sure on him to in effect comment on what other people have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not really. He doesn't have to comment. He can just tell the Trial Chamber what his vision of the correct facts is, as far as is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes well, that might be right. And with a case of a strong witness, that's often the case if Your Honours please. I'm just a bit concerned, though, that effect might arise, that he's being asked the comment on what someone else says. I don't see any problem with Mr. Lazarevic saying to him? Look, "it was Jovo Savic who said this, you're wrong. And what you do you say about that." There's no problem with that. And I don't see why he can't ask it or frame it in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think Mr. Lazarevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I can reply very briefly because that is my last question actually. Our dear colleagues from the Prosecution always push us in about asserting to the witness the Defence of our client. And when we do that, they object and say okay. Now you ask him to comment this and this. I already said that I spoke to my client and that he said that he possibly was there but it wasn't him actually who held that speech, that there was the gentleman Jovo Savic was the one who held the speech. And so this is exactly what I did now. And I really don't believe that there are any reason for our colleagues to object to that. Of course, I mentioned that this -- there were other witnesses who also stated that it was that gentleman, but basically this is the defence of my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. I think the exchange is sufficient. We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Any other counsel wishing to cross-examine? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Dagovic. I am Dragan Krgovic, and I will ask you a number of questions relating to your testimony in chief, and I will also touch upon some topics that you have already mentioned. You will agree with me that Bosanski Samac before the outbreak of the conflict was a multi-ethnic community.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Members of all the three predominant ethnic communities -- Muslims, Serbs, and Croats -- lived there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any ethnic tension before the 17th of April, 1992 in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any clashes between members of different ethnic communities?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And a certain amount of tension?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been. I'm not very well informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Any events that might have disturbed the citizens of Bosanski Samac, such as clashes between armed men, wounding of members of the 4th Detachment, putting up of barricades, establishment of armed patrols? All of these were developments prior to the outbreak of the conflict on the 17th of April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did it occasionally happen that members of all the three ethnic groups sent their families away or left together with their families for a while?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We'll move on to another topic. When you testified, you described among other things the arrival of Miroslav Tadic on the 18th of April, 1992 to the yard in front of your house. Apart from that occasion on the 18th of April, 1992, in the period that you spent in Samac how often did you see Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say precisely how many times I saw him, but it was very frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was it 10, 15 times?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been more often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony on the 18th of April, on page 7175 of the transcript, you said that Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric were standing on the tank that stopped in front of your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When we got out into the yard, when we were called out, they were standing there. The tank was parked, and they were standing on the tank. They couldn't have been standing on it if the tank had been moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You described how Miroslav Tadic wore a leather raincoat and had a beard.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your interview with the OTP -- in fact, in your testimony in chief, you said that he had a long beard. It wasn't very clear then. How large was this beard?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say it was large. It was trimmed, a normal beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So it had been grown for a while.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was very well kept, trimmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It takes a while to grow such a beard, three or four months, would you say?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he also wear glasses?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, small round eyeglasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the time when you used to see Tadic in town, he had a beard.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all the time. But on that day when he came, on the 18th of April, he had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said at one point that you had seen Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric entering the retirement home.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have a beard then, Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Relative to the 17th of April, when you saw Miroslav Tadic, until, let's say, December 1992, in that period when you used to see him, did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you he didn't have a beard the whole time, but on the 18th of April he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But when you came to see him and inquire about the possibility of getting exchanged, did he have a beard then?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that summer when you saw him, during the summer did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We'll move on to something entirely different. You said that just after the 17th of April, a courier summoned you to the building of the TO to the assembly. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that citizens were also invited to gather in front of the Buducnost factory in those -- during those days?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend that assembly in front of the Buducnost factory?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that on that occasion outside the Buducnost factory, there were members of all the three ethnic communities, Serbs, Muslims, and Croats?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the Serbs. I know that there were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone for counsel. The question was not recorded or heard.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel, the interpreters said they hadn't got your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were there members of other ethnicities apart from these Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any of your neighbours, fellow townsfolk, Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember anyone making a speech at that assembly and issuing an order?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a speech. But I don't know who made it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what it was about? Was there an agreement announced or an order issued?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know what had been agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the immediate reason for that gathering?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If I told you that this gathering discussed the fact that an armed conflict had broken out and that all able-bodied citizens should take part according to their abilities, either in the army or in terms of work duty, would you agree that that was discussed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In response to one of the Prosecutor's questions you said that the ban on gathering of two or more Muslims and Croats was something you heard about two or more months after the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. About two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That makes it sometime in June.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, that means that it was allowed in the first two months after the 17th of April to assemble with members of your own ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was there an event that caused this ban perhaps?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was there an incident or an attack, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Document P40 that was shown to you by the Prosecution is dated 4th of August, 1992. If you don't remember it, we will ask the usher to show it to you again.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you claim that this announcement was made on the radio a considerable time before you learnt about this -- before this ban.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was announced on the radio, and only later posters were put up around town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this order with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Posters were put up all around town, everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you see it for the first time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I saw it after about two months. It was -- the posters were all over town. The order was all over town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So this information from the poster, you knew about it from the radio; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So in fact, if I understand you correctly, the way you understand it, so this was just a repeat order from the radio.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So I don't find it very logical. So perhaps if you know, was this order repeated because it wasn't respected and that's why the posters were put up, or perhaps there's another reason that you know of? Perhaps you could clarify this lack of logic.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the reason is, why this order was repeated. I don't know about it. I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was this order respected?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know about someone who did not respect this order?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was anyone punished because they didn't respect this order?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were there other orders that were issued that you heard about on the radio and that they were later put on posters?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you tell me, this order that was shown to you by the Prosecutor, that is the order that you saw at that time in Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's a copy of that order -- that that's order; right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned in your testimony that there was an order that there should be white armbands worn; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was this also broadcast on the radio, this information?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And were there posters?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no posters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How long was this obligation for, that people should wear white armbands?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were you wearing a white armband?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We all had to wear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you. I don't know exactly. Perhaps for four or five months. I'm not sure exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: While you were doing your work obligation.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the beginning, I had to wear this white armband in the work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about later?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later I did not. Whether this was abolished later -- later we did not wear the white armband.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you tell me whether the soldiers were wearing white armbands in those first few days in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you call them members of the 4th Detachment, those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And who did it relate to, this order?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How did you find out about the order?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was broadcast on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any sanctions? Were there any penalties if anyone was not wearing a white armband?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That person would probably be arrested. I don't know. The order was respected. It had to be respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone was arrested because they didn't wear an armband or suffer any sanction?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether anyone was arrested because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, when you gathered in front of the retirement home to get the work task, there were mostly Muslims and Croats there; right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And how many of you were there in that group?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were up to 50, 60 of us. That depended. All people who were able to work -- all those people were able to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: From when? Could you tell me from which period? When did you start your work obligation? When did you start going to work?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of days after the takeover of the town. Very quickly afterwards we were sent to forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you had work obligation until December 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And there were more than three Muslims or Croats in one place during this period.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone come, a soldier or policeman, to warn you that you should not be gathering more than three in one place?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that's different. This ban on relation to town -- but we were there working at work obligation. So this did not -- did not relate to us, to us working. It only was valid for the town, that people in the town were not supposed to gather more than three Muslims or Croats in the town. It did not apply to the forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that this ban on gathering just applied to people who could be a threat to safety?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it applied to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You gathered in front of the retirement home.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Dzevad Celic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was his office located on the ground floor of the retirement home?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go into his office?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where did he come out when he came to give you your tasks?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Celic never gave me any tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But to read some kind of information, or anyone that was supposed to read some -- something on the work obligation, where did they come out of?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Nothing was ever read out to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go upstairs in the retirement home?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, during the break the Defence photographed together with the investigators -- we photographed the retirement home, that is, its surrounding area, the interior, and also where this premises were that witnesses so far have spoken about. So I would like to ask for the permission of the Trial Chamber to show these photographs to the witness which he can just clarify some details. I have already handed over these photographs to the Prosecutor's office, and I believe that there would be no objections to us showing it. And I do have enough copies for everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, do you know this building?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What is pictured on this building?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the lower part was the retirement home. And upstairs were apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So what you mean by the retirement home, when you say "retirement home," and that we gathered -- when you say "we gathered in front of the retirement home," this is this room to the right, on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The entire ground floor was the retirement home, this premise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, these photographs are not marked to assist us to look at the correct one when they are being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be number 1. This paragraph here would be number 1. And all the others as they come, they would get -- they'll get the numbers that follow. But if I could be -- I could be given a number for identification, if there are no objections to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Why don't we -- why don't we approach it in this way, if Your Honours please. Perhaps counsel could show the witness the photograph, we could also see it on the ELMO, could get the witness to describe it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Say what it depicts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And then when that's occurred, he could tender it fully into evidence. There won't be an objection so long as the witness identifies and says this is something I know about and I can comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I've go no objection now having heard what he said for this photograph depicting the retirement home to go fully into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes can we have the number as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be D36/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just ask for it to be entered into the transcript that the witness identified this building as the facility at -- whose ground floor was the room where the retirement home was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark with an arrow on this photograph -- perhaps you could just mark perhaps with an "X" exactly where the premises of the retirement home were.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark with an arrow where the entrance to the premises of the retirement home is.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you if you could next to the arrow put number "1," and next to the cross a mark of number "2," please, with the marker on the photograph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So next to the arrow number ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Number "1."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we go through this again. It's a bit confusing. The arrow shows what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The entrance -- the entrance to the premises of the retirement home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And that's the one you want him to mark number "1."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, number 1. While number 2, the actual premises, the entire ground floor, which is occupied by the retirement home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Do you think, counsel, that afterwards he could point to them with the pointer? Because there's a lot of glare on my screen in front of me and I can't really see the arrow very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think using the ELMO. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the entrance to the retirement home. While the entire ground floor, this is where the premises of the retirement home were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can I just ask one question to the witness. So as far as you know, the offices of the retirement home were only on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, as far as I know it was only the ground floor. Upstairs were all apartments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So, counsel, maybe you could find out from the witness -- when we're talking about a retirement home, that sounds as though it's a residential place where senior citizens are residing. Is that the case, or is it a place where retired persons congregated during the day, a community centre for retirees?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You heard Judge Williams. I presume that perhaps we both know what this is. So this is the premise that was used by pensioners, by their -- for their activities, where they gathered, play chess, cards, and so on. So this was used as recreation.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there were offices, this part above the retirement home, and that at some point before the 17th of April they were premises of the local commune?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I don't know what was located above.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know that there was another entrance from which you can go to the offices upstairs?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm finished with this photograph. Could you please show photograph number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, if you look at it, you can see -- perhaps I could suggest that there is -- there is a pole on which you're supposed to put a flag. Is that correct? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the same building, this retirement home?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, when you used to come in front of the retirement home when you came for your work obligation, did you see there that there was a Red Cross flag by any chance?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you put a circle on that photograph. Could you just put a circle around that, around these poles that are used for flags.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is just for the transcript, that the witness identified a base for flag poles on this building that we will continue to call the retirement home, since this is the term that we've used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am finished with that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Before you do, could you ask the witness to tell us what the wording means to the right of the flag pole. We can see the name of the town, of course, "Bosanski Samac." But there is something above that that might be useful for us to know what it says, in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you read what it says here on the photograph. If I tell you that it says "local commune, Bosanski Samac," do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It says, "Local commune, Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Could we have a number for this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D37/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you were never in this office, in these premises above the retirement home while you were in Samac from the -- after the 17th of April, 1992 until you left in December 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was never on these premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, since you mentioned in your testimony earlier that your mother and yourself, that you went to put your name down for an exchange. Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the building where Social Services used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Pere Bosnica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That is in your street?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me who did you go to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Sveta Vasovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go and see him?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion. But on several occasions, to Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Vasovic's office in this premises of Social Services that we spoke about?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Anka Jovanic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about Dusanka Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Velja Mastic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was a director of the Social Services, of that institution that you went to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that this was Social Services, or was this Red Cross, this institution that you went to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that in that building until the 17th of April, there was the Social Services premises. But what happened -- what was -- what else was located there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These premises that are shown on the photograph, you don't know about them. I'll tell you. These are photographs. This corridor is above -- located above the retirement home in the local commune. So you were never there and you don't know anything about this premises.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know them, and I was never there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion when you went to see Miroslav Tadic, he was sitting in this office in the Social Services building; right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This building has several storeys, several floors. Can you just describe it for us?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a -- it has just one floor. It's one upstairs. So there just are no other floors. It's just one floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where was Miroslav Tadic seated? Where is his office?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly as you go in. He was in that building. He had his office in that building there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about Sveto Vasovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was he in that building?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was in that building. He was not in the same office as Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours, please, I'm not objecting to this evidence at all. But I think that we should all be clear so -- I hope I'm not experiencing -- the only one experiencing difficulties. Is the witness talking about the Social Services building just off his own memory and describing offices there, or is he referring to the photograph when he talks? I'm just not clear about all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't know if he's acknowledged that this is the -- this shows the interior of the Social Services building or whether he's not acknowledging that. I think we ought to be clear, because it's still on the ELMO, and I -- I'm a little uncertain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, counsel. You can clarify with the witness what this photograph on the ELMO now depicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us if you know this office that -- on this photograph that you see.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These are not the offices of the Social Services that we spoke about earlier.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they're not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I no longer need this photograph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have it marked for -- as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could it be marked as a -- merely as a -- for identification at this stage. I mean, if witness doesn't know what it is or says -- maybe another witness at a later point will be able to come along --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You -- okay. So you're raising an objection to this one now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: To this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the witness doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: He doesn't know. Someone else may know, so we'll be able to have it in as a full exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification only. Can we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D38/3 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to the retirement home. When you used to come in front of the retirement home, who gave you instructions as to where to go? Who organised -- who organised you all here on the actual site? Who led you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who organised it. I don't know who organised it. But I know that when I was working in Grebnica I know the entire time I was led there by Milo Zaranic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Dzevad Celic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was he also involved in this work obligation in some way? Did he do anything? Did he participate, or was he kind of a clerk?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he did. While I was in forced labour, he did not work with me. Perhaps he worked somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him in front of the retirement home?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. On a couple of occasions I saw him in front of retirement home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he give you any instructions, tasks? Did he explain anything to you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who told you what you were going to do on such and such a day, what work obligation you would do, whether you would go to, for instance, Grebnica? Are you going to go to a farm, are you going to collect firewood, are you going to go and do agricultural things? Who you give you these instructions?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you. While I was in Grebnica, instructions were given by Mile Zoranovic, because he had already made the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And who showed you this list?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mile Zoranovic. He would come out in the street. He would read the list of names. They would be loaded onto buses -- onto the lorry and then they would go and work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know Bozo Ninkovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did Bozo Ninkovic give you any instructions or perhaps to the people who led you to the work obligation?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about those people who led you to your work obligation?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You remember as you were asked by my colleagues that you gave a statement to the Prosecutor's office in September 1994?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, you told them what you knew and what you had indirect knowledge of; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, presumably your memory was fresher, since this was just prior to that that you had left the former Yugoslavia, and you gave them the -- your knowledge or information correctly.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you signed that statement?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in general terms, it is correct what is written in that statement.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general terms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will now read a portion of your statement. Now, for the -- for my colleagues from the Prosecution, because the versions in B/C/S and English differ in pagination, so that would be on page which is marked by number 00182961, the last paragraph, which continues onto the next page. "Bozo Ninkovic, representative of the Ministry of Defence of Bosanski Samac, for the Serbs. He was also the one who was in charge of giving the work orders for the forced labour. I know that he is the one giving the orders because he gave orders to the people picking us up for work. They always had a piece of paper with his signature on it." Do you remember that you stated this?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. It was eight years from that. So it's hard to remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is this correct, what you stated?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this piece of paper with your signature on it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This paper which had orders for forced labour, if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Further on, when you were speaking about the work obligation, you spoke before this Trial Chamber on page 7212 that you were involved in gathering firewood and distributing it to the citizens of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that firewood that you took, you also took to the families of people who were killed in battle or people who were wounded in battle?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know that first what we distributed, firewood and fuel, that was always to the Serb families. It was possible that these were families of fallen soldiers. But they were certainly of Serb ethnicity, these families.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, these citizens did they sign for that fuel, for that firewood that they received?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that they signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was an organised signing for firewood for all ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know whether in the organisation of the Red Cross, there was distributed milk and bread to all citizens in all areas?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was in the beginning. That was for about two or three weeks and then it stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I presume that after that, there were milk shops and bread shops were working. Bakeries and perhaps there was a shortage of food perhaps. Do you know the reason?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the reason why that stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony before this Chamber, you said that you were working as a seasonal worker on agricultural lands.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Asked by Judge Williams whether these were -- what kind of farms these were, you said that these were mostly state-owned farms.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. These farms before the war were state owned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of work did you do? What kind of jobs?

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the farms?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SAFET DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had to feed the cattle, clean the farms, do all the jobs that need to be done on a farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
